footnotes.text: These five books (Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy) are also called the Pentateuch—a Greek word meaning “the fivefold book” (Bible Dictionary, “Pentateuch”). Jewish people refer to these books as the Torah or the law of Israel (see Guide to the Scriptures, “Pentateuch,” Gospel Library). The Bible itself does not identify who wrote the Pentateuch. Many scholars believe that there were multiple writers, editors, and others involved in producing the text we have today (see Avram Shannon, “Authorship,” inOld Testament Cultural Insights, ed. Taylor D. Halverson [2022],https://biblecentral.info/library/chapter/authorship/). For example, the book of Genesis in its current form can be dated back to the Jewish exile in the sixth century BC (see Michael D. Coogan and others, eds.,The New Oxford Annotated Bible: New Revised Standard Version, 5th ed. [2018], 6). Regardless of the complexity involved in the creation of the Pentateuch as we have it today, Restoration scripture confirms Moses’s central involvement in these works of scripture (see1 Nephi 5:10–11;Moses 1:40–41;2:1).
